claims.text: Pulumi programs that treat an Output<T> as a plain value can produce placeholder text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` in log lines, generated files, or resource properties instead of the expected value.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ ("Output value errors") exists and describes this and other symptoms of treating an output as if it were already a plain value.
The exact placeholder message text is `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`.
The Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/output-values/ exists and covers diagnosing errors from stringifying, branching on, or reading a Pulumi output value like a plain value.
Pulumi Cloud returns a "409 conflict: Another update is currently in progress" error when an update conflicts with an in-progress update.
The page /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ exists.
Pulumi Cloud can return 500 internal server errors.
When the CLI can't access a self-managed (DIY) state backend, it produces a `read ".pulumi/meta.yaml"` error, documented at the anchor #error-reading-pulumimetayaml in the using-a-diy-backend page.
Crashes or hangs on Apple Silicon can be caused by x86_64 binaries running under Rosetta 2.
A recently deleted stack can be recovered from the Pulumi Cloud console, including after an accidental `pulumi stack rm --force`.
Pulumi supports `--target` and `--exclude` options to limit operations to specific resources.
Pulumi provides automatic logging, CLI verbose logging, and program logging for debugging, documented in the logging page.
Pulumi dev builds are pre-release builds that provide bug fixes not yet shipped in a stable release.
Running `pulumi logs share` securely sends the logs from a failed operation to the Pulumi team.
`pulumi destroy` can fail, and Pulumi documents scenarios for handling this.
The logging page has a #cli-verbose-logging anchor, and #automatic-logging anchor (L115).
Pulumi offers a Community Slack at slack.pulumi.com for community support.
Pulumi resource properties are represented as Outputs rather than plain values because their real values are not known until the providing resource has been created or updated.
Representing resource properties as Outputs is central to how Pulumi builds a dependency graph and runs `pulumi preview`.

When an output value is concatenated, logged, or converted to a string directly instead of via `apply` or an equivalent helper, Pulumi does not raise an error by default and silently substitutes a placeholder message for the value.
In TypeScript, converting an Output to a string yields literal text such as `Calling [toString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `apply` or `pulumi.interpolate`.
In TypeScript, calling `JSON.stringify()` on an output, or letting one flow into a JSON body, produces a `Calling [toJSON] on an [Output<T>] is not supported` string rather than the value.
In Python, converting an Output to a string via f-string yields literal text such as `Calling __str__ on an Output[T] is not supported`, and Pulumi also logs a warning.
In Python, passing an output to `json.dumps()` fails with `TypeError: Object of type Output is not JSON serializable`.
In Python, `Output.json_dumps()` is the Pulumi method to use to serialize outputs to JSON.
In Go, passing a `pulumi.StringOutput` where a `string` is expected is a compile error, and values are resolved with `ApplyT`.
In C#, converting an Output to a string yields literal text such as `Calling [ToString] on an [Output<T>] is not supported`, followed by guidance to use `Apply` or `Output.Format`.

Setting the environment variable `PULUMI_ERROR_OUTPUT_STRING=true` (supported in TypeScript, Python, and C#) makes the string conversion of an output throw an exception at the point of the mistake instead of returning placeholder text.

The string-composition helpers for outputs are `pulumi.interpolate` and `pulumi.concat` in TypeScript, `Output.concat`/`Output.format`/`Output.json_dumps` in Python, `pulumi.Sprintf`/`pulumi.JSONMarshal` in Go, and `Output.Format` in C#.
Docs pages exist at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/apply/ and /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/all/ covering accessing single outputs with apply and working with multiple outputs.
A docs section on Outputs exists at /docs/iac/concepts/inputs-outputs/#outputs.

The `apply` callback runs asynchronously once the output resolves, generally after the program's top-level code has finished, so an outer variable assigned inside the callback is still undefined when read outside it.
The apply callback runs when the engine resolves the dependency graph, not on the program's clock, so adding a delay does not fix the issue.
Most Pulumi resource inputs accept outputs as well as plain values, while a handful of positions such as a resource's logical name cannot.
In a dynamically typed language, an `if` on an output object is generally always true because the Output object itself is evaluated, not its eventual value.
In statically typed languages, branching on an `Output<bool>` is usually a compile error because an Output<bool> is not a bool.
A stack configuration value read with `pulumi.Config`, an environment variable, or a hardcoded flag is a plain value that can be branched on normally.
Passing an output as a resource's logical name or loop bound or map key fails to compile in TypeScript, Go, and C#.
In Python, passing an output as a resource's logical name raises `TypeError: Expected resource name to be a string`.
In Python, using an output as a loop bound (`range(some_output)`) raises `TypeError: 'Output' object cannot be interpreted as an integer`.
In Python, using an output as a dictionary key does not raise; Python falls back to comparing and hashing the output object itself so the lookup silently keys on the wrong thing.
A StackReference can be used to consume a first stack's outputs in a later separate stack; a docs section exists at /docs/iac/concepts/stacks/#stackreferences.

Pulumi has no supported way to block a program and synchronously extract a resolved value from an output; awaiting or reading an output synchronously either doesn't compile, fails at runtime, or returns placeholder text.
`pulumi stack output <name>` reads a single stack output from the CLI after a deployment.
The Automation API exposes an `outputs` field on the result of running an update (e.g. `res.Outputs` in Go), and a docs page exists at /docs/iac/concepts/automation-api/.
